### A-ECO-01: No paid randomised rewards (loot boxes)

**MUST** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Detection: static · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** No loot boxes, gacha, mystery chests or other variable rewards that can be obtained with money or with currency purchasable with money.

**Why.** KIDS Act Art. 13(2) bans variable reward systems on social and video services. DFA proposal bans paid loot boxes for minors in games.

**How to improve.** Replace with fixed, visible rewards earned through learning.

**Sources.** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [DFA](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/09/eu-to-blacklist-ten-manipulative-online-design-traps-leaked-draft-shows)

### A-ECO-02: No pay-to-win

**MUST** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Detection: mixed · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** Nothing bought with money gives a gameplay or learning advantage.

**Why.** DFA proposal bans pay-to-win for minors. Fairness in learning.

**How to improve.** Make all progression earnable through play; keep any paid items cosmetic and adult-purchased.

**Sources.** [DFA](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/09/eu-to-blacklist-ten-manipulative-online-design-traps-leaked-draft-shows), [UCPD](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2005/29/oj)

### A-PLY-02: Non-shaming failure and feedback

**SHOULD** · Level 3 (Best practice) · Age bands: all · Detection: manual · Effort: low

**Requirement.** Errors and failures are presented as part of learning, without ridicule, sad animations directed at the child, or public exposure.

**Why.** Psychological safety supports learning, especially for younger children.

**How to improve.** Review all failure states with an instructional designer; use encouraging, specific feedback.

**Sources.** [UNCRC-GC25](https://www.ohchr.org/en/documents/general-comments-and-recommendations/general-comment-no-25-2021-childrens-rights-relation), [ARNAB2014](https://doi.org/10.1111/bjet.12113)

### B-DAT-01: Research use of learning data is separated

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Detection: manual · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** Learning data is only shared for research under a data sharing agreement, with legal basis, ethics approval and pseudonymisation, and never as a by-product of normal operation.

**Why.** GDPR Art. 5(1)(b), 6 and 89.

**How to improve.** Create a research export pipeline that pseudonymises and logs every extract.

**Sources.** [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)

### B-EVL-01: High-risk path for systems that evaluate or place learners

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Features: ai_assessment, ai_adaptive · Detection: manifest · Effort: high

**Requirement.** AI that evaluates learning outcomes, steers learning, assigns levels or monitors tests is treated as an Annex III high-risk candidate: risk management file, data governance, logging, human oversight, accuracy and robustness testing.

**Why.** AI Act Annex III(3). Obligations apply from 2 Dec 2027 under the Digital Omnibus.

**How to improve.** Open a risk management file now (templates/ai-risk-file.md) and record the classification decision.

**Sources.** [AIA](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj), [AIA-OMNIBUS](https://www.gibsondunn.com/eu-ai-act-omnibus-agreement-postponed-high-risk-deadlines-and-other-key-changes/)

### B-EVL-02: No camera-based or biometric proctoring of minors

**MUST** · Level 1 (Legal baseline) · Age bands: all · Features: assessment, ai_assessment · Detection: static · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** Tests are not proctored by webcam, eye tracking, keystroke biometrics or behaviour analysis of the child.

**Why.** AI Act Art. 5(1)(f) (emotion recognition) and Annex III(3)(d) (monitoring during tests). GDPR Art. 9.

**How to improve.** Use supervised test conditions in class instead of automated surveillance.

**Sources.** [AIA](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj), [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)

### B-EVL-03: Results are explainable and contestable

**MUST** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Features: assessment, ai_assessment · Detection: manual · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** Teachers and learners can see why a result was given and can contest it with a human.

**Why.** GDPR Art. 22(3). AI Act transparency for high-risk systems.

**How to improve.** Show per-item evidence behind each score and a 'request review' action for teachers.

**Sources.** [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj), [AIA](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj)

### B-EVL-04: Validity, fairness and accessibility of assessment

**SHOULD** · Level 3 (Best practice) · Age bands: all · Features: assessment, ai_assessment · Detection: manual · Effort: high

**Requirement.** Assessment validity is documented, results are checked for bias across groups (gender, language background, SEN), and accommodations (extra time, audio) do not disadvantage learners.

**Why.** Good assessment practice and AI Act data governance expectations.

**How to improve.** Run a differential item functioning check on pilot data and document accommodations.

**Sources.** [AIA](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/1689/oj), [UNCRC-GC25](https://www.ohchr.org/en/documents/general-comments-and-recommendations/general-comment-no-25-2021-childrens-rights-relation)

### B-OPS-01: Dashboards show learning, not surveillance

**SHOULD** · Level 3 (Best practice) · Age bands: all · Detection: manual · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** Teacher and guardian dashboards show what helps learning; they avoid minute-by-minute activity logs and are explained to the child.

**Why.** Respect for the child's privacy and agency (KIDS Act Art. 20(1)(f), UN GC 25).

**How to improve.** Aggregate activity data and show learning progress instead of raw logs.

**Sources.** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [UNCRC-GC25](https://www.ohchr.org/en/documents/general-comments-and-recommendations/general-comment-no-25-2021-childrens-rights-relation)

### B-SIM-01: Sensitive simulations include warnings and debrief

**SHOULD** · Level 3 (Best practice) · Age bands: all · Detection: manual · Effort: low

**Requirement.** Simulations about health, conflict, loss or other sensitive themes include a content note, an exit at any time, and a guided debrief.

**Why.** Protects children from distressing content and supports reflection.

**How to improve.** Add content notes and a debrief screen designed with the instructional team.

**Sources.** [UNCRC-GC25](https://www.ohchr.org/en/documents/general-comments-and-recommendations/general-comment-no-25-2021-childrens-rights-relation), [DSA-G28](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/commission-publishes-guidelines-protection-minors)

### B-UGC-01: User-generated content is moderated and visible to the teacher

**MUST** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Features: ugc, chat · Detection: mixed · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** Content created or uploaded by children is moderated proportionally to age, visible to the responsible teacher, reportable, and not public. Uploaded media has metadata (e.g. GPS) stripped.

**Why.** DSA Art. 28 guidelines. KIDS Act Art. 12(3) and 19.

**How to improve.** Add teacher review queues, EXIF stripping on upload, and keep galleries class-private.

**Sources.** [DSA-G28](https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/library/commission-publishes-guidelines-protection-minors), [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)

### B-UGC-02: No photos of children's faces kept or shared beyond need

**MUST** · Level 2 (Forward-compliant) · Age bands: all · Features: ugc · Detection: manual · Effort: medium

**Requirement.** Photos and videos of children are only stored when necessary for the learning activity, are never public, expire automatically, and others cannot download them.

**Why.** KIDS Act Art. 12(3)(e). GDPR minimisation and storage limitation.

**How to improve.** Prefer avatars; add auto-expiry and disable download of child media.

**Sources.** [KIDS](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX:52026PC0681), [GDPR](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2016/679/oj)
